{{Short description|Type of integer sequence}}
{{No footnotes|date=September 2025}}
In mathematics, a '''divisibility sequence''' is an [[integer sequence]] <math>(a_n)</math> indexed by [[positive integer]]s {{mvar|n}} such that

:<math>\text{if }m\mid n\text{ then }a_m\mid a_n</math>

for all&nbsp;{{mvar|m}} and&nbsp;{{mvar|n}}.  That is, whenever one index is a multiple of another one, then the corresponding term also is a multiple of the other term.  The concept can be generalized to sequences with values in any [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] where the concept of [[divisibility]] is defined.

A '''strong divisibility sequence''' is an integer sequence <math>(a_n)</math> such that for all positive integers&nbsp;{{mvar|m}} and&nbsp;{{mvar|n}},

:<math>\gcd(a_m,a_n) = a_{\gcd(m,n)},</math>
where {{math|gcd}} is the [[greatest common divisor]] function.

Every strong divisibility sequence is a divisibility sequence: <math>\gcd(m,n) = m</math> if and only if <math>m\mid n</math>. Therefore, by the strong divisibility property, <math>\gcd(a_m,a_n) = a_m</math> and therefore <math>a_m\mid a_n</math>.

==Examples==
Any [[Lucas sequence]] of the first kind {{math|''U''<sub>''n''</sub>(''P'', ''Q'')}} is a divisibility sequence. Moreover, it is a strong divisibility sequence when {{math|1=gcd(''P'', ''Q'') = 1}}.  Specific examples include:
* Any constant sequence {{tmath|1=a_n = k}} is a strong divisibility sequence, which is {{math|''kU''<sub>''n''</sub>(1, 0)}} for {{math|''n'' ≥ 1}}.
* Every sequence of the form {{tmath|1=a_n = kn}}, for some nonzero integer {{mvar|k}}, is a divisibility sequence.  It is equal to {{math|''kU''<sub>''n''</sub>(2, 1)}}.
* The [[Fibonacci numbers]] {{math|''F''<sub>''n''</sub>}} form a strong divisibility sequence, which is {{math|''U''<sub>''n''</sub>(1, −1)}}.
* The [[Mersenne number]]s <math>a_n = 2^n-1</math> form a strong divisibility sequence, which is {{math|''U''<sub>''n''</sub>(3, 2)}}.
* The [[repunit]] numbers {{math|''R''{{supsub|(''b'')|''n''}}}} for {{math|1=''n'' = 1, 2, ...}} in any base {{mvar|b}} form a strong divisibility sequence, which is {{math|''U''<sub>''n''</sub>(''b'' + 1, ''b'')}}.
* Any sequence of the form <math>a_n = A^n - B^n</math> for integers <math>A>B>0</math> is a divisibility sequence, which is {{math|(''A'' − ''B'')''U''<sub>''n''</sub>(''A'' + ''B'', ''AB'')}}. If <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> are coprime then this is a strong divisibility sequence.

[[Elliptic divisibility sequence]]s are another class of divisibility sequences.
